text: Kristina of the Woods was a planeswalker native to Corondor on Dominaria, whose planeswalker's spark manifested after the creation of the Shard of the Twelve Worlds.
Lacjsi was the commander of the Knights of Thorn during the Dark Age on Dominaria.

Kiel was a brother of Brion Stoutarm and Rosheen Meanderer. He was said to have some prophetic talents, which is not surprising given that Rosheen was the most renowned giant oracle on Lorwyn. He was quite silent and thoughtful. Brion and Kiel were once hired by Rhys to help eliminate a boggart raiding party. Rhys was then ordered by Nath to send the giants away, but they refused to leave until the work was done. In the end, they agreed to leave if Rhys brought stories to their sister, who should be present at the Aurora celebration in Kinsbaile. Rhys later met the giant brothers near Kinsbaile. However, the group was ambushed during their talk by the Gilt Leaf pursuit commando, and both wer

Kula was an anchorite (a form of religious hermit and druid) from Dominaria. She was six and a half feet tall, with a broad skull and nut-brown skin, and dressed like a jungle dweller, in leather skins, carrying bone fetishes. Kula was very good at spotting lies.
Shaper Kopala, Warden of Waves, is a introspective wizard of the River Heralds on Ixalan. He is the youngest of the Nine Shapers.
Klothys is the God of Fate and Destiny on Theros. She is associated with red and green mana.
Kwain is a rabbitfolk wizard from Bloomburrow who first appeared in Commander Legends.
Killian Lu is a human mage-student in his second year at the Silverquill College at Strixhaven University on Arcavios. He is called Killy by his friends.
Leighbet is a former Izzet inventor who discovered a way of administering electrical immunity.
Kitsa is a legendary otter wizard from Bloomburrow and an Otterball Elite.
Kolevi of Havenwood was an Elder Druid from Havenwood on Dominaria.

Lim-Dûl (/lɪm dul/ LIHM-dool) was a powerful necromancer who terrorized Terisiare during the Ice Age. The fragment of his essence contained within the Ring of Mairsil is known as The Raven Man. He conducted two major campaigns to take over the mana-rich plane of Shandalar and orchestrated Liliana Vess's procurement of the Chain Veil.
The Lord of House Khone was a black-mana wizard knight of the Black Fortress in Arathoxia (Dominaria). He was also lord of House Khone of Khone Keep in the Khone swamp of Golthonor on Corondor.
Dr. Ludevic of Ulm is a wheezing and reclusive necro-alchemist, and the most influential of Innistrad's merchants.
Maga (MAH-gah; ) was a Wizard from the Minamo on Kamigawa, with a passion for oni magic.
Licia, Sanguine Tribune is a legendary vampire soldier from an unknown plane.
M'Odo, the Gnarled Oracle, is a zombie elf wizard from an unknown plane.
Lucia Covi is an assassin who works for Marchesa d'Amati on the plane of Fiora.

Masrath is a planeswalker from Dominaria who ascended when the Mending occurred. Masrath is a hot-headed, impatient mage, with a potent smile and nose for trouble that landed him in hot water too many times to recount. He was a school friend of Tessebik. When they met again on their home plane, they decided to travel together to a new plane that neither of them had been to before, Ravnica. They would each spend a few days exploring the lands, assimilating creatures and phenomena into spells, and seeking out new forms of magic native to that plane. Then they'd face off right there, on that plane, to see how sharp each of them had become in the nine years they had spent apart.
Great Maha, also known as the Great-Night Owl, the Night Owl, the Eclipse Owl,, and the Season of Long Night is an antagonist on Bloomburrow in the Dragonstorm Arc. It is a major Calamity Beast.
Mardia is a vampire cleric stationed at Adanto, the First Fort, part of the Legion of Dusk on Ixalan.

Merieke Ri Berit was a mysterious figure who lived during the Ice Age in Terisiare on Dominaria. Little is known about her, save that she was a temptress who used magical powers to ensnare other creatures. Her race is in doubt; she is officially noted as a human, but her art depicts her as an elf.
Melek is a weird wizard of the Izzet League on Ravnica. He was chosen as the Izzet maze runner. He was reforged sometime around the time Murders at Karlov Manor took place.

Meren, of Clan Nel Toth, is a human necromancer from the shard of Jund on the plane of Alara. After her exile and attempted murder among her kin, she fled to the shard of Grixis, which converged upon Jund after the Conflux and began to learn the art of raising the dead.
Morgane, the Great Druid was a druid on Shandalar, who took command of the Green Guild until its downfall.
Noranda-Zang was a wizard who ruled the land of Everlorne on an undisclosed plane.
Tacenda Verlasen is a songmage and possible planeswalker from Innistrad.
Tariel, Reckoner of Souls, is a legendary angel from an unknown plane.
Terrik is an elven wurmcaller, part of the Selesnya Conclave on the plane of Ravnica.
Terashi (tair-ASH-ee / teh-RAH-shee) is a kami from Kamigawa. It is the great kami of the sun.

Tomik Vrona is a law and security mage from Ravnica. He is chief advokist of the Orzhov Syndicate, and the former apprentice of Teysa Karlov. He served as acting guildmaster after the War of the Spark, but has since become second to Teysa.
The Unluckiest is an unnamed planeswalker from an undefined plane, who is cursed with bad luck.
Timothar Markov is a vampire noble from Innistrad belonging to the Markov bloodline.
Tomoya (TOH-moh-yah) the Revealer was a human wizard from Kamigawa who was active during the Kami War.
Vaylesh, known as the Ebon Hand Priestess, was a high priestess in the Order of the Ebon Hand on Sarpadia (Dominaria).

Ulasht is a legendary hydra that inhabits the ruins of Ravnica left behind by the Gruul Clans. Ulasht is unique in that its multiple heads are hellions, a worm-like creature with tentacles surrounding a tooth-filled mouth. Though not officially a part of any clan, it is revered by many Gruul as a natural embodiment of pure destruction and mindless rage.
Uyo (OO-yoh; ) was the greatest of soratami seers and prophets, and one of the highest-ranked persona in the soratami hierarchy on Kamigawa.
Boss Uramon was a criminal overlord in the Takenuma swamp on Kamigawa.
Vannemir was a Terisian warrior who was raised from the dead to fulfill his destiny and save his world from being destroyed by Heidar.
Veko is a spirit priest aligned with the Orzhov, known for his role in manipulating life and death.
Virot Maglan, the Cabal Patriarch (also known as The First of the Cabal) was the leader and founder of Dominaria's Cabal.
Vorel of the Hull Clade is a human / merfolk hybrid biomancer from the Simic Combine on Ravnica.

Winota, Heartbonder is a human warrior on the plane of Ikoria. Winota is one of the bonders, humans who form magical connections with the monsters of Ikoria. She told the planeswalker Vivien Reid how she lost her right arm trying to kill the monster that she ended up bonding with. Now Winota and her companion (which resembles a huge plated raccoon) travel Ikoria helping other bonders and monsters learn to fight side by side.
Vito Quijano de Pasamonte was a heretical vampire hierophant of the Church of Dusk who worshipped Aclazotz on the plane of Ixalan. He was granted demonic power by his god before his death.
Volpaig was a bishop of the Church of Avacyn, and secretly the leader of the Skirsdag Cult on the plane of Innistrad.

Worrin Betzold was a human bishop, and the father of Dennick Betzold. After his death he became a zombie, mindlessly still preaching his sermons to the undead hordes swarming Thraben. He was a native of Gavony, Innistrad.
Vytas was a noble and an Umbris cultist from Traublassen, Innistrad.
Zakk was a wizard of unknown origin who fought Kazz, as mentioned in the Rivals Quick Start Set. She also appeared in the Summer Magic intro along with her rival.
Zahid is a djinn from Dominaria. He has blue skin, glowing blue eyes, pointed ears, tattoos, black hair, black eyebrows and a long thin moustache. Sometimes his hair changes into black smoke.
Champion Zahur is a leonin zombie warrior charioteer from Amonkhet. He originates from the lost era before Nicol Bolas.
Alniul, the Twice Whisperer, is a human shaman from Tarkir and the head whisperer of the Temur Frontier.
Fumulus, also known as the Infestation, is a vampire insect from an unknown plane.
The Haunt of Hightower is a legendary Moroii vampire from Ravnica.
Ivora, also known as the Insatiable Heir, is a vampire warrior from an unknown plane.

The Immortal Faller, variously called the Dweller, the One Who Sounds in the Deep, Him Who Falls, The Seeker in the Well, or simply the Faller is the savior and first prophet of the Monoist faith in the Edge.
Kolodin is a human triumph mage from Kylem. He was co-captain and mechanic of the Cloudspire Racing Team in the Ghirapur Grand Prix.
Dr. Ludevic of Ulm is a wheezing and reclusive necro-alchemist, and the most influential of Innistrad's merchants.
A Master of the Hunt is a human demigod who has developed a particular type of bond with a specific type of animal on Dominaria.

Mica is a Lorehold student, artificer, and geomancer, at Strixhaven University on the plane of Arcavios. He demonstrates an exceptional affinity for stone and earth, with minimal aptitude for spiritual magic, and exhibits limited social engagement, often focusing exclusively on physical surroundings and geological phenomena rather than talking with fellow students or professors.
Dean Moseo is an owlin skeleton warlock teacher at the Witherbloom College of Strixhaven University on Arcavios.
Plagon, also known as the Lord of the Beach, is a starfishfolk wizard from an unknown plane.

Alameda Slim, more simply by his surname Slim, and also known as Yancy O'Del in disguise, is the main antagonist of Disney's 2004 animated feature film Home on the Range. He is a feared, wanted cattle rustler who is said to be capable of stealing 5,000 cattle in a single night, and has the ability to entrance cattle through his yodeling, which he utilizes in his thefts.

Alacazar is a supporting character who appears in the Sofia the First and Elena of Avalor crossover special, Elena and the Secret of Avalor. He is the former the Royal Wizard of Avalor, and the grandfather of Mateo.

Ana Helstrom is one of the main protagonists of the Marvel Hulu series Helstrom. By day, Ana runs a successful auction house and suffers no fools, but her true interest lies in protect the innocent from the forces of evil. Ana is driven to rid the world of demons. She is portrayed by Sydney Lemmon. Ana Helstrom was created by Roy Thomas and John Romita Sr.

Alma Madrigal (often referred to as Abuela) is the deuteragonist of Disney's 2021 animated feature film Encanto. She is a wise old woman who was blessed with a gift-granting Miracle Candle, Abuela is the matriarch of the Madrigals, the mother of Julieta, Pepa, and Bruno, and the grandmother of Isabela, Dolores, Luisa, Camilo, Mirabel, and Antonio. As the original source of its magic, Abuela also serves as the head of the enchanted village in which she and her family resides.

Annihilus is a Marvel Comics supervillain who appears in the Disney XD animated series The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes. He is an insectoid dictator who hails from the Negative Zone. Annihilus was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

The Hedge Witch, known as Andrea Sage under the Dark Curse, is an antagonist on the ABC show Once Upon a Time. She is a member of the Coven of the Eight, who was cursed to live in Hyperion Heights. She debuts in the tenth episode of the seventh season: "The Eighth Witch".

Angie, also known as The Alien Scout and Grandma Angie, was an alien who made her debut in Zombies 3. She was the scout of the aliens, until she crashed on Seabrook, on Planet Earth. She was Addison Wells' and Bucky Buchanan's maternal grandmother.
Aphroducky is a goddess of love that appears in "A DuckTales Valentine". She becomes struck by one of her arrows and falls in love with Scrooge McDuck.

Antonio Madrigal is a major character in Disney's 2021 animated feature film Encanto. He is the youngest son of Pepa and Félix Madrigal, and the younger brother of Dolores and Camilo. Antonio is gifted with the power to communicate with animals.
Aphrodite is a recurring character in the third season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians, and is the Goddess of Love and beauty. She is also the mother of Aidan.

Asteroth is an evil wizard from the Mighty Ducks TV series. He is from another dimension, which is actually a supernatural version of Anaheim, California. His title is "Lord of the Red Dragon", since he can morph into a large red dragon when enough power is in his possession. The Ducks fight him twice: first in the alternate Anaheim, and then in the "real" Anaheim. He is a member of the Royal Immortal Knights.

Atticus Thorn is the primary antagonist of the 2003 video game The Haunted Mansion, which is based on the Disneyland ride attraction and the movie of the same name. He is the leader of an evil secret society known only as the Order of Shadows, an ancient cult obsessed with destroying all that is good and just in the world.
Bananas B. is a magical talking monkey from the animated television series American Dragon: Jake Long.

Ayo is a Marvel Comics character that appeared in Captain America: Civil War, Black Panther, Avengers: Infinity War, The Falcon and The Winter Soldier, and Black Panther: Wakanda Forever. She is portrayed by Florence Kasumba. Ayo is a member and the second-in-command of the Dora Milaje, the elite team of enforcers tasked to protect T'Challa and Wakanda. She is kind, noble, brave, and loyal to the ruler of Wakanda. She is a skilled strategist and politician and an expert at hand-to-hand combat. Ayo was created by Al Ewing and Kenneth Rocafort.

Baymax is the deuteragonist of Disney's 2014 animated feature film Big Hero 6. He is an inflatable computerized robot created by Tadashi Hamada to serve as a personal healthcare companion. Following Tadashi's death, Baymax was inherited by Hiro Hamada, with whom he became a member of the superhero team known as Big Hero 6. He is based on the Marvel character of the same name from the Marvel Comics series, Big Hero 6. Baymax was created by Scott Lobdell and Gus Vazquez.
Bess is the art-talent fairy at Tinker Bell's Pixie Hollow. While she's the best artist around, when she starts painting, look out! Things can get messy pretty quick.
The Cauldron Born, also known as the Army of the Dead, are the undead minions of the Horned King from Disney's 1985 animated feature film The Black Cauldron.

Cassandra Eleanor "Cassie" Lang, is a Marvel Comics character who first appears in Ant-Man. She is the daughter of Scott Lang, whom she views as a hero, even before he takes on the mantle of the superhero. Later, she exposes herself to Pym Particles and becomes the superhero Stature. Cassandra Lang was created by David Michelinie and John Byrne.

Charles De Girl is a character in Valiant. She is a member of the French Residence: Mouse Division and a master of disguise. She and Rollo guided Valiant and the Royal Homing Piegeon Service through the battlefield to get the message.

The Coven of the Eight are characters featured in the ABC series Once Upon a Time. They make their first appearance in the Season Six finale, "The Final Battle Part 2". The coven are a team of evil witches, who are feared and dreaded, and considered to be the "worst of the worst". They're behind the curse that transported several residents of the Magical Forest to Hyperion Heights, and are lead by Gothel.

Amy Hall, better known as DNAmy, is a minor villain from the animated television show Kim Possible. Amy is the world's foremost engineer in genetics, with a special talent for gene-splicing. She is also an avid collector of Cuddle Buddies, a line of collectable stuffed animals generally consisting of two different animals combined into a single plush toy.

The Cy-Bugs are the secondary antagonists of Disney's 2012 animated feature film Wreck-It Ralph. They are a race of viral, cybernetic, bug-like creatures that serve as the generic enemies in the game Hero's Duty. Unlike other characters in the arcade, Cy-Bugs are unable to tell the difference between the game and real life, meaning that they are truly malevolent creatures. Their only instincts are to eat, kill, and multiply their swarm, while their greatest weakness is any beacon of light. The soldiers of Hero's Duty remain in constant battle with the bugs, to prevent them from escaping the game, taking over the arcade, and destroying every game in their wake.
Dae is a character who appears in Zombies: The Re-Animated Series. She is a quirky and adorkable witch who adds a touch of magic to the already eclectic group.

Darby Steel is a character in the 2022 Disney•Pixar animated film Lightyear. She is a gruff, no-nonsense, and not-exactly-voluntary member of the Junior Zap Patrol. She was doing time in prison until she joined the unit in exchange of having her sentence reduced. Darby is known to be an explosives expert, who can take any device and turn it into something that will blow up.

Denis Webber, also known as the Delivery Man is a character in the Marvel Cinematic Universe featured in the Marvel Disney+ series WandaVision. He is amongst the many residents of Westview, who become entrapped, when Wanda unleashes chaos magic, barricading the town, and transforming everything within, into a sitcom. In this new world, he is assigned the identity of Dennis the Mailman He works in the neighborhood of Wanda and Vision. As each episode passes, Dennis adapts into a new time period. After the Westview's sitcom reality reaches the mid-to-late 2000s, Dennis becomes assigned to Dennis the Delivery Man. He makes his debut in the first episode and is portrayed by Amos Glick.

Doctor Octopus (real name Dr. Otto Gunther Octavius), or simply Doc Ock, is a fictional supervillain in Marvel Comics. He appears in Spider-Man: No Way Home, portrayed by Alfred Molina, reprising the role from the 2004 film Spider-Man 2. Dr. Octavius is a brilliant Oscorp scientist that created mechanical, intelligent tentacle-like arms, but suffered a lab accident. He survived his injuries and became a villain equipped with the arms, who is confronted by Spider-Man from his universe. Doctor Octopus was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.

Dominic was an evil wizard and the nephew of Gorog. He was the main antagonist of The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex. He was an evil wizard who was killed by Mason Greybeck, Alex's boyfriend, who pushed Dominic off the Tower of Pisa.
Double Dan is a minor character of Disney's 2018 animated feature film Ralph Breaks the Internet. He is a slug-like creature who is a virus creator.

Commander Drex, or simply known as Drex, is the main antagonist in the movie Super Buddies. He is a body possessing alien that wants the power rings of Inspiron for his own purposes to create an empire of his own ideologies.

Dr. Minutia is a one-shot villain on Teamo Supremo, first mentioned in the episode "Calling Captain Excellent!" and later featured in the episode "Micro Supremo!" He is Captain Excellent's archenemy, whose weapon of choice is his Reduct-o-Ray, which, as the name suggests, shrinks anyone zapped by it. In his single appearance on the show, Dr. Minutia learns that Captain Excellent, who is currently off battling Big Skull, has left his Hyper-Michronic Device at Level 7, so he plans to steal it. When Teamo attempts to stop him, he and his valet, Cosmo, shrink them with his Reduct-o-Ray. With Teamo detained, Minutia makes his way to the state capitol and also uses his Reduct-o-Ray on Governor Kev

Dr. Mary Beth Evilini is an evil Wizard and former professor at WizTech. She planned to take the winner of a competition of the Twelve Balls to a volcano and steal their powers for her own. She is played by Octavia Spencer.

Dr. Vile is an antagonist in Disney's The Little Mermaid series. He appeared as the main antagonist in the episode "Island of Fear". He is the former employer of Daniel who loves experimenting on crabs and turning them into crab mutant monsters.

Dr. Wilfred Nagel is a Marvel Comics character in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, who appears in the Disney+ series The Falcon and The Winter Soldier. He makes his only appearance in the third episode and is portrayed by Olli Haaskivi. Dr. Nagel is responsible for recreating the super soldier serum, which grants individuals enhanced abilities. He initially worked under HYDRA, until it fell. Nagel was one of the many individuals to disappear during the Blip, and when he returned, he resumed his work under the Power Broker in Madripoor. He was interrogated by the Falcon, the Winter Soldier, and Baron Zemo, in his laboratory, where he was killed by the latter. Dr. Nagel was created by Robert Mor

Edgar is a character from Disney's 2022 animated/live-action feature film, Disenchanted. He is a barista at the coffee shop in Monroeville. He is somehow able to know someone's orders before they make them. Malvina Monroe claims that he is her "eyes and ears". When he is infected by Giselle’s wish to live a fairytale life and Monroeville turns into Monrolasia, he is transformed into Malvina's magic mirror.

Electronique is a minor character in the television series Kim Possible. She is a villain of Go City who is able to utilize the power of electricity and use it for her own nefarious purposes. She is also one of the many adversaries of Team Go, a team of superheroes devoted to the protection of Go City.
Edgar Volgud is an antagonist in Atlantis: Milo's Return. He is allied with the Krakken, being somehow able to control the creature.
Elijah Price is the main antagonist of the M. Night Shyamalan films: Unbreakable and Glass. He lives with Osteogensis Imperfecta and a supervillain of sharp intellect.
Edward "Evil Ed" Lee is a supporting character, later villain, of the 2011 Touchstone Pictures film Fright Night. He is Charley Brewster's former best friend who gets turned into a vampire.

Emma Swan is the main character and protagonist of the first six seasons of Once Upon a Time. She is the daughter of Snow White and Prince Charming and the older sister of Neal Nolan. She is the mother of Henry Mills and Hope and the wife of Captain Hook. She was sent to the real world after the Evil Queen placed a terrible curse upon the Enchanted Forest. She worked at a bail bonds agency while living in Boston until her son, Henry Mills, found her and brought her to Storybrooke to break the curse. Unfortunately, she is absorbed into a vortex of pure evil, which makes her become the new Dark One in the place of Rumplestiltskin, acting as the main antagonist in Season 5A until the episode "B

Emma Graves is a character who appears in the supernatural teen drama series Coven Academy. Miss Graves is a witch and the high-principled principal of Crescent Veil Academy, who was once a student herself, alongside Briar's mother, Mary.
Facilier's Shadow is a supporting antagonist in Disney's 2009 animated feature film The Princess and the Frog. He is a sentient shadow belonging to Dr. Facilier, serving as his sinister sidekick.

Fibber, also known as Experiment 032, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to detect lies; the more individuals lie, the more he buzzes, forcing entire populations to tell the truth. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".
Fenrir is a minor villain in Hercules: The Animated Series. He is the Harbinger of Ragnarok.

Fang (real name Fred Sykes) is a major antagonist and apparently a human mutate from the Disney animated series Gargoyles. Beginning in the episode "Metamorphosis", he, along with Claw and Talon, are revealed by a mad scientist named Anton Sevarius. While Fang is apparently a despicable thug, the others (Maggie, Claw, and Talon) are actually heroic.

Fall-Apart Rabbit is a friend of Bonkers D. Bobcat who appeared in the Bonkers episodes directed by Robert Taylor. He is a yellow bunny with detachable body parts (somewhat like Oswald the Lucky Rabbit), and as his name suggests, they tend to fall off easily. In the series, Fall-Apart worked as Bonkers' stunt double at Wackytoons Studios until his show was cancelled. He mostly appears in the Lucky episodes, as his final appearance was in "New Partners on the Block" episode.

Finder, also known as Experiment 158, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to sniff out and uncover any lost or missing individual or item like a hound dog; he can also fly by spinning his ears like helicopter blades to ensure optimal tracking potential. Upon success, he honks like a party blower. His one true place is operating a "Lost and Found" service at the beach.

Gorgon is a member of the Inhuman Royal Family. As a result of being exposed to the Terrigen Mist when he was an infant, Gorgon developed hooved feet and a powerful lower body. His legs are so powerful that with a single stomp, he can create shock tremors to disable his opponents. Gorgon was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

The Green Army Men (also called Bucket O' Soldiers) are supporting characters in the Disney•Pixar Toy Story franchise. They were Andy's 200 miniature green plastic soldiers, led by Sarge. They are set in particular positions and stuck to bases (however, this does not slow them down) and are stored in a bucket labeled Bucket O' Soldiers. The soldiers are quite disciplined with a "leave-no-man-behind" policy and are masters of reconnaissance. Woody describes them as "professionals".

Grogu is the deuteragonist of the Disney+ Star Wars series The Mandalorian. He is a Force-sensitive 50-year-old infant of the same species as Yoda who is sought after by the Bounty Hunters' Guild on behalf of the Imperial remnant. He is taken in by Din Djarin as a Mandalorian foundling and adoptive son. He is later briefly taken by Luke Skywalker to be trained in the ways of the Force, but he ends up rejecting the Jedi path and decides to return to his adoptive father.
The Gray Sisters are supporting characters in the Disney+ series Percy Jackson and the Olympians. They are prophetic sisters who drive a taxi cab.

The Hag and the Werewolf are minor antagonists who appears in the 2008 Disney/Walden Media adaptation of The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian. They are two former servants and worshipers of Jadis the White Witch intent on using cunning an manipulation to resurrect her from the dead.

Heckler, also known as Experiment 322, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to undermine enemy morale with verbal abuse. His one true place is in a dunk tank, provoking people to try and dunk him.
Hekapoo is a character who appears in the Disney XD animated series Star vs. the Forces of Evil. She is the forger of Dimensional Scissors and one of the members of the Magic High Commission.

Hiro Hamada is the protagonist of Disney's 2014 animated feature film Big Hero 6. He is a fourteen-year-old robotics prodigy living in San Fransokyo under the care of his aunt and older brother Tadashi. After Tadashi's sudden death at the hands of a kabuki-masked villain, Hiro—with support from his healthcare companion, Baymax—became the founder and leader of Big Hero 6. Hiro was created by Scott Lobdell and Gus Vazquez.

Hunkahunka, also known as Experiment 323, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to cause societies to come to a crashing standstill by causing artificial lovesickness. Once he pecks someone, they fall in love with the first individual they see regardless of their gender, species, and personal preferences; only spraying water in the victim's face will break the spell. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".
Hugin and Munin are Asgard's two ravens who serve as the eyes and ears of Odin. This version of the mythological Hugin and Munin was created by Roy Thomas and John Buscema.

Hunter (formerly known as The Golden Guard) is a major character in The Owl House. He is a grimwalker created by Emperor Belos who served as his assistant, believing he was a powerless witch and Belos' nephew before discovering the truth. He is now one of Luz's closest friends and allies who helps her in her fight against Belos.

Imager is a minor character of the Disney Channel original series, The Villains of Valley View. She is a supervillain from Centropolis and a member of the League of Villains. She is portrayed Chanel Casteñeda.

Isaiah Bradley is a Marvel Comics character who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He makes his debut in the Disney+ series The Falcon and The Winter Soldier. Isaiah is a super soldier, who was secretly granted his abilities. He fought Bucky Barnes, during the Korean War, and was one of the few soldiers to best him which garnered him a fearful reputation, by HYDRA, to the likes of Captain America. Isaiah Bradley was created by Robert Morales and Kyle Baker.

Alfred T. Slipper, better known as "Incandesto", is a character who appears in the 2021 Disney+ original film Flora & Ulysses. Created by George Buckman, he is a superhero who appears in a comic of the same name written by George himself; however, since George faced writer's block, he was unable to get his stories published, resulting him to face challenges throughout his life.
Isaiah Howard is one of the five main protagonists from the first season of Goosebumps. He is a high school football player who encounters a mysterious camera that predicts terrible futures.
Isabella Chen Lopez is one of the five main protagonists from the first season of Goosebumps. She is an introvert who finds empowerment from a mask that begins to alter her mind.

Jake Madden is one of the main protagonists of the Disney Channel original series, The Villains of Valley View. He is a supervillain, posing as an ordinary boy. His supervillain name is Chaos. Like the rest of her family, besides Vic, Jake has superpowers and is a full blown villain. He is portrayed by Reed Horstmann.

Harold Jay Smith, better known as Jay Silverheels, was a Canadian actor, athlete, stuntman, poet, and salesman, descended from three Iroquois nations. For Disney, he appeared in the Walt Disney Presents serial "Texas John Slaughter", Smith!, and One Little Indian. Born in Canada, on the Six Nations of the Grand River reserve, near Hagersville, Ontario. He was a grandson of Mohawk Chief A. G. Smith. His father was wounded and decorated for service at the battles of Somme and Ypres during World War I, and later was an adjutant training Polish-American recruits for the Blue Army for service in France, at Niagara-on-the-Lake, Ontario. Excelling in lacrosse, he travelled throughout North America

Jake Dawson is one of the main characters who appears in the supernatural teen drama series Coven Academy. Jake is a warlock and student at Crescent Veil Academy. Having not had a father figure in his life, he finds himself gravitated towards his teacher Mr. Cole for guidance and support. He also falls for new student Briar when she begins attending the academy.

The Jesters (named Harlequin, Lollipop, and Tricksy) are a trio of magicians and the secondary antagonists of Disney's 1998 animated sequel, Pocahontas II: Journey to a New World, the sequel to the 1995 animated feature, Pocahontas. They are Governor Ratcliffe's minions.

Jod Na Nawood is the hidden main antagonist in the live-action Star Wars Disney+ limited series Star Wars: Skeleton Crew. He is a Force-sensitive pirate with a dozen alias who encounters a group of lost children from the planet At Attin. He strikes a deal with them; offering to get them home in exchange for a reward. In truth, At Attin is reputed to be the location of an immense treasure horde, which Jod seeks for himself.

John Slade is the main antagonist of The Shaggy D.A. He is the corrupt district attorney who is Wilby Daniels' opponent for the upcoming election for District Attorney. He comes into possession of the Borgia Ring and uses it to change Wilby into a dog.
Lew Zealand is a humanoid Muppet who is a boomerang fish thrower. He throws the fish away, and they come back to him.

Link, also known as Experiment 251 and Linkenstein, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to bind together incompatible individuals so that their arguing causes massive chaos. His glue has indestructible function qualities on fifty different planets (excluding Earth); the only thing that can make it dissolve is mud. His one true place is working at the Cliff Diving for Couples attraction, teaching arguing couples to do things together by using his binds for bungee jumping.

Lilia Calderu is a Marvel Comics character, who makes her live-action debut in the Marvel Cinematic Universe Disney+ series Agatha All Along. Lilia was an ancient Siclilan witch who performed fortunes and was recruited by Agatha Harkness to join her new coven to watch the legendary Witches' Road, where Lilia met her demise after defeating the Salem Seven. Lilia Calderu was created by Steve Englehart, Mike Friedrich and Frank Brunner.
Little Witch Rosita, more commonly known as Rosita, is a witch from Goldie & Bear in "Training of the Broom".

Lorider, also known as Experiment 047, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to publicly humiliate victims by pulling down their pants (hence the name Lo-Rider). Jumba would often release him in crowds and meetings. He appears in the Stitch! anime.
The Magus is a character from the Disney animated TV show Gargoyles. He was the court magician of Castle Wyvern, and eventually became Princess Katharine's top advisor.

Erik Magnus Lehnsherr, known as Magneto, is a major character of Marvel Comics. He is a powerful mutant and supervillain, being an enemy to the X-Men. Despite this, Magneto is also the old friend and rival of Professor X and the two of them will often put their differences aside and work together depending on the circumstances. Magneto was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

Madame Placebo is a one-shot character who appears in Adventures of the Gummi Bears. Her only appearance is in the episode "Tummi Trouble". A Lotion and Potion Gypsy by trade traveling through Drekmore, she is responsible for giving Igthorn a love potion, to be used on Lady Bane. After the scheme goes awry, and Bane accidentally falls in love with Toadwart, while Tummi falls in love with Bane, Igthorn catches up with Madame Placebo around Dunwyn forest, in order to find out how to break the spell again.

Magik is a Marvel Comics character who appeared in The New Mutants, played by Anya Taylor-Joy. She is Colossus' younger sister, and her nature as a mutant gives her access to magic, which she uses to great effect, as she is an expert sorceress. Magik was created by Len Wein and Dave Cockrum.

Mar-Vell is a Marvel Comics character. She is a Kree who invented faster-than-light travel as a means to benefit the universe. When the other Kree decided to use her invention to further the genocide of the Skrull, she realized the true evil nature of her fellow Kree and sacrificed her life to keep her invention out of the hands of the Kree. Mar-Vell was created by Stan Lee and Gene Colan.

The Master Control Program (usually abbreviated as MCP) is the main antagonist of the 1982 Disney film Tron. It was a computer program created by Ed Dillinger that ruled inside ENCOM's mainframe computer to overview the game system, but rebelled itself and decided to get rid of the humans (users, as it usually refers to them). During the rule of the MCP, many programs were enslaved and pitted against the program's henchmen, led by Sark.

All info provided by Master Sensei at Kim Possible Wiki Master Sensei is the head teacher of the Yamanouchi Ninja School in Kim Possible. He has many different skills and he has mastered Levitation and Astral Projection.
Marlin is a wizard fish who only appeared in "Of Myths and Mermaids", the final issue of Marvel Comics series of The Little Mermaid.

The Marvels are a trio of super heroines, compromising of Captain Marvel, Monica Rambeau, and Ms. Marvel, first appearing in the 2023 Marvel film The Marvels. The three are brought together after finding themselves in a quantum entanglment, switching places with the other, every time one of them uses their powers. The trio unite to end their entanglement, and defeat Dar-Benn, the cause of their predicament, who is set on revenge against Captain Marvel.

Mego is a minor character in the animated Disney Channel television series Kim Possible. He is one of the members of Team Go, he's younger than Hego and older than the Wego Twins; although it is unclear if he is the same age or older than Shego. His power in Team Go may be an allusion to the Mego line of action figures in that he can shrink to the size of one.
Miles is a main character of the Disney Channel Original Movie Avalon High. He is the reincarnation of Merlin.
Misty the Wonderful Witch is a recurring character from the Disney Jr. television series Jake and the Never Land Pirates.

Captain Monica Rambeau is a Marvel Comics character who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. She made her debut in the 2019 film, Captain Marvel, and returns as a starring character, in the first Marvel Disney+ series WandaVision, before returning in The Marvels. As a child, she was portrayed by Azari and Akira Akbar, in Captain Marvel, and was succeeded by Teyonah Parris, who goes on to portray her as an adult. She is the daughter of Air Force captain Maria Rambeau, and a close friend to Captain Marvel. She later goes on to become a S.W.O.R.D. agent, following in the same career as her mother, who founded the organization. Monica was amongst the many victims of Thanos' snap, and was br

Moon Girl (real name Lunella Lafayette) is a superhero from Marvel Comics. She makes her debut as the eponymous protagonist of the Disney Channel series Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur. She has a brilliant scientific mind that lets her invents gadgets that she uses to fight crime and protect the innocent alongside her best bud, Devil Dinosaur. Moon Girl was created by Amy Reeder, Brandon Montclare, and Natacha Bustos.
Morgana Macawber is a character from the Darkwing Duck TV show and comic books. She is a Transylvanian sorceress, and the love interest of Darkwing Duck.

Mr. Fantastic (real name: Reed Richards) is a Marvel Comics character who is the leader of the Fantastic Four, and one of the most brilliant scientific minds. Mr. Fantastic was created by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby.

Mr. Beaver is a character who appears in the 2005 Disney/Walden Media adaptation of The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, who helps the Pevensie siblings bring Narnia back to its beautiful self. He knows that the White Witch would deceive people and knew that before the Pevensie's knew it.
Mr. Medulla is a science teacher at Sky High in the 2005 movie of the same name. He has a massive skull due to being super intelligent. He was portrayed by Kevin McDonald.

Ms. Marvel (real name Kamala Khan) is a superheroine from Marvel Comics who appears within the Marvel Cinematic Universe. She makes her debut as the protagonist of the 2022 Disney+ series, Ms. Marvel and is portrayed by Iman Vellani. Kamala is a Pakistani-American teenager, who was granted powers after inheriting a mystical bangle from her grandmother. She unlocks her latent abilities whilst attending AvengerCon, and begins training as a superhero, with the help of her friend, Bruno Carrelli. During her adventures, she comes into conflict with a group of Djinn, known as the Clandestines, and learns more about her family lineage, and the source of her powers. Kamala later becomes quantumly en

Mr. Woodbird is a woodpecker, who is the janitor at T.O.T.S. He takes care of maintaining T.O.T.S. HQ, as well as managing the park outside. He enjoys inventing things that can make things easier for the fliers or K.C. in the nursery. He loves making loves for the babies the most. He enjoys eating sandwiches while he works. He has a habit of adding long numbers to his inventions even if they're the first one of the kind. He sometimes gives someone his inventions even if he hasn't tested them out himself. He also loves babies a lot like everyone at T.O.T.S. He achieved his dream of delivering a baby and seeing the happy parents in Season 2.
Penn Zero is the titular main protagonist of the 2015 Disney XD animated series Penn Zero: Part-Time Hero. He is a student at Middleburg Central High, who also works as a part-time hero.

Pinky is a recurring character of Disney's television series, Phineas and Ferb. He is Isabella Garcia-Shapiro's pet chihuahua. Though by outward appearance he is a mindless animal, it has been revealed that he, like Perry the Platypus, is a secret agent (specifically in Wanda's Division). He, like Perry, is codenamed Agent P, but is more commonly referred to as Pinky or Agent Pinky. His nemesis is Professor Poofenplotz.

Pix, also known as Experiment 214, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to take bad pictures of individuals. His one true place is with Mrs. Hasagawa as one of her "cats".

Princess Jun is the Princess of Wei-Ling and a minor character from Sofia the First. She is a good friend of Princess Sofia, Princess Hildegard, Princess Amber, Princess Clio, and Princess Vivian. Her parents are Emperor Quon and Empress Lin-Lin, her little brother is Jin, and they are the Imperial Family of Wei-Ling. Jun has a very good memory, recalling old stories from her mom and able to describe the various statues in her garden. She's a very talented bamboo flute player, able to even calm down lagoon lizards and get a ride from them. She has a playbook for Dazzleball in her possession that she tried to get Amber to read and usually failed to her annoyance.
Quentin Beck (also known as Mysterio) is a Marvel Comics former supervillain who appears in the animated series Ultimate Spider-Man. Quentin Beck was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.

Queen Narissa is the main antagonist from Disney's 2007 hybrid film Enchanted. She is Prince Edward's stepmother, the ruling Queen of Andalasia and an evil sorceress with a hatred for Giselle, who she tries to kill multiple times with help from Nathaniel.

Rani is the most passionate water-talent fairy of all. She loves rainy days and splashing in puddles. She even knows how to whistle mermaid songs. Her favorite dreams are swimming dreams. Rani can do amazing, magical things with water: bounce it like a ball, mold it into the shape of a fish, or scoop it up in her fingers without losing a drop. She can also help her fellow fairies with water-related things, such as getting water to boil faster. Rani is the only fairy in Pixie Hollow who can swim. This is because she has no wings. She sacrificed them on the quest to save Mother Dove's egg. She's not entirely unhappy about losing her wings since she had always longed to swim, though she misses

Radioactive Man (real name Dr. Chen Lu) is a radiation-based Marvel character who appears in The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes. Radioactive Man was created by Stan Lee, Robert Bernstein and Jack Kirby.

Raven Lydia Baxter is the titular and iconic protagonist of Disney Channel's That's So Raven and its second spin-off Raven's Home. She is the daughter and oldest child of Tanya and Victor Baxter. She is Cory Baxter's older sister. She is Nia and Booker Baxter-Carter's mother.
Ghost Rider (real name Robbie Reyes) is a supernatural entity originating from Marvel Comics as a superhero, by possession of a human host. Ghost Rider was created by Felipe Smith and Tradd Moore.
Robot Ray is a major character from Doc McStuffins. He is Donny's toy robot who has robot vision, a sticky rope and a little light on top of his head.

Roxanne Parks is the mother of Chyna and Cameron Parks and the wife of Darryl Parks. She is portrayed by Elise Neal. She's a children birthday parties entertainer. In "SciANTs Fair", Darryl called to her, but she wasn't seen. She made a cameo in the pilot episode. She appeared in the episode "ClairvoyANT" as an astronaut for a party. In "FraudulANT", Paisley and Lexi auditioned for her to become Birthday-Party entertainers. In "MutANT Farm" she is implied to be a gorgon. She later appeared in "SANTa's Little Helpers", in which she admitted that she disliked her sister. She most recently appeared in "PerformANTs", where she went with Chyna and her friends to a concert.
Rumble is the main antagonist of the Disney Fairies television special Pixie Hollow Games. He is a storm-talent sparrow man.
Ruben Chen is the secondary antagonist of the second season of The Ghost and Molly McGee. He is the father of Ollie and June and husband of Esther who leads his family in hunting ghosts.

The Sanderson Sisters are the main antagonists of the 1993 live-action film Hocus Pocus and its 2022 sequel Hocus Pocus 2. They are a trio of witch sisters who were the most powerful coven that ever lived, thanks to Winifred's book of spells. In the first film, they were accidentally revived by Max Dennison in modern-day Salem and attempt to become immortal by consuming the life force of children using their Life Potion. In the sequel, they sought to cast a spell that would make them all-powerful so they could have their revenge on Salem.

The Scroll is a supporting character from Disney's 2022 animated/live-action feature film, Disenchanted. He is a magic scroll that helps Giselle and Malvina Monroe. When presented, the Scroll was inanimate, but after Giselle makes a wish on the Andalasian Wand of Wishes for a fairytale life transforming Monroeville into Monrolasia, he comes to life.
Shakata, Razili, and Farida, also known as the Witches of the Sand, are the main antagonists in the Aladdin episode "Witch Way Did She Go?"

Shortstuff, also known as Experiment 297, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to sabotage mechanical devices; specifically, he is naturally drawn to electrical machinery, which he then shorts out to create utter chaos. Due to him being accidentally enlarged, his one true place is as a carnival ride.

Shoe, also known as Experiment 113, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to generate negative events; however, adjusting his cranial horseshoe controls the type of event (luck) generated. In a downward position, he causes bad luck; in an upright position, he causes good luck. His one true place is at the mini-golf course, making miniature golfers score holes-in-one.

Shiriki Utundu is the main antagonist of Tokyo DisneySea's version of the Tower of Terror. He is a cursed [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nkondi nkondi] idol and is responsible for the disappearance, and supposed death, of Harrison Hightower III.

Sidon Ithano is an male alien who appears in the Star Wars sequel trilogy. He commands Maz Kanata's pirate clan and leads them in defense of her secret fortress. He has the ability, as is common with his species, to mimic sounds.

Princess Shuri (also known as Black Panther) is a Marvel Comics character who appears in both the Marvel Cinematic Universe and in Marvel Animation. She is the Princess of Wakanda, the daughter of King T'Chaka and Queen Ramonda, and the sister of T'Challa. She has genius-level intellect, being on the same intellectual level as Tony Stark, Hank Pym, and Bruce Banner. Shuri loves her brother deeply and, with her extreme scientific knowledge, she helps not only Wakanda as a whole but also T'Challa in his role as a superhero. After her brother's passing, Shuri assumes his role, taking on the mantle of Black Panther. Shuri was created by Ben Dunn and Reginald Hudlin.

Slick, also known as Experiment 020, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to sell anything to anyone like an expert by using his sales pitch and auctioneer-like stratagems. However, once he starts selling, he is programmed to do it nonstop. His one true place is selling for charity and fundraisers at Lilo's hula school.

Skunkuna is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jacques von Hämsterviel and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise, first appearing in the Stitch! anime. He is designed to launch out spheres of pink repulsive odors from underneath his fur and is susceptible to Mr. Stenchy's charms, something that Jumba's other experiments are immune to. When his odor is mixed with Mr. Stenchy's, it can incredibly be used as an air freshener.

Sisu is the deuteragonist of Disney's 2021 animated feature film Raya and the Last Dragon. She is a divine water dragon who is revered across Kumandra for her role in vanquishing the Druun with the magic of a Dragon Gem. When the Gem is fragmented across Kumandra’s five lands, Sisu is summoned by Raya, a warrior princess, to restore its power and save humanity.

Solomon the Great is said to be the wisest Dinosaur of them all. He was voiced by Michael Dorn, his body is puppeteered by [http://muppet.wikia.com/wiki/Jack_Tate Jack Tate] and his face was operated by Bruce Lanoil. He appeared in the Dinosaurs episode "[http://muppet.wikia.com/wiki/Episode_211:_Switched_at_Birth Switched at Birth]" as a way to settle the custody of Baby Sinclair and Aubrey Molehill once and for all. Initially, he wore a robe, looking as if he was going to perform some ancient ritual, but he removed his robe and appeared in [http://muppet.wikia.com/wiki/Magicians magician] attire. His plan on settling custody of the babies was to cut them in two halves and give one half to

Spats, also known as Experiment 397, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to cause local populations to argue with each other so they do not notice someone taking over their planet. If the afflicted individuals count to ten, their belligerence will dissolve. His one true place is with Wizard Kelly, making his professional wrestlers fight more convincingly.

Sphinx Martindale is a minor character from the Hercules TV Series. He is a game-show loving creature with the body of a lion, the head of a man, and bird wings who lives high up on a mountain top. Whenever someone trespasses on his domain he forces them to play on his game show and if they answer all his questions right he gives them a fabulous prize but if they get them wrong he eats them.

Stamen, also known as Experiment 103, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to intercept and prevent pollination by attracting bees and other pollinators to himself instead of flowers. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".

George "Sticky" Washington is the deuteragonist in the Disney+ series The Mysterious Benedict Society. He is an overly cautious boy who has the ability to remember everything that he reads and expounds a vast array of knowledge and skills.
Tamaa is a character who appears in the Disney Jr. animated series The Lion Guard. He is a greater racket-tailed drongo who can, like most of his kind, mimic the voices of many different animals.

Tech (birth number CT-9902) is a minor character in Star Wars: The Clone Wars and one of the tritagonists in Star Wars: The Bad Batch. Tech is a genetically defective clone of Jango Fett and a member of Clone Force 99, also known as the Bad Batch, a squad of clone commandos who each bore genetic mutations, Tech's mutation is enhanced intelligence, large deposit of technology, and knowledge.

Tchotchke Jones is a villain from the Hamster & Gretel episode "The Bottle Episode". He's the owner and shopkeeper of a small store in town called Tchotchke's Tchotchkes, which, as the name states, sells a variety of trinkets. He's also an avid collector of impossible bottles, some of which are put on sale in his shop. He has been shrinking various landmarks from around the area (including most recently, the riverboat The Muddy Bess) with a shrinking ray that instantly puts targets in a bottle, using a poorly designed mask to conceal his face.

The Grim Reaper (otherwise known as Death) is a legendary figure being the personification of death. Best known to be described as a skeleton in a hooded cloak (that usually hides their face) carrying a scythe. The Grim Reaper has appeared in many Disney properties. He first appeared in the 1929 short The Haunted House as the overarching antagonist and leader of the Skeletons.

The Krylock Demon is a fictional creature from the animated series American Dragon: Jake Long. It was a beast of pure evil which feeds off of magical creatures, such as Unicorns. It had the head of a cobra and the body of a scorpion. It was also inter-dimensional, meaning that it lived in another dimension. The only way it could come to Earth is if it passed through a dimensional door, which could pop out anywhere at anytime. Because of this, it was impossible to track. Its home was a wasteland of lava and rocks, possibly the interior of a volcano or a place similar to the Underworld.

Mukhtar is a recurring character in the Disney animated series Aladdin. He is the last surviving member of a race of Mukhtars, otherwise known as Genie hunters, and therefore was originally Genie's enemy until he later reformed and they became allies.
The Skeleton King, usually just referred to as Skeleton King, is the main antagonist of the Jetix original series "Super Robot Monkey Team Hyperforce Go!". His servants include the Formless.

Theodora the Wicked Witch of the West is the secondary antagonist of Disney's 2013 fantasy film Oz the Great and Powerful. A witch to be feared, she is Evanora's sister. With her natural gaze, she truly believes that Oscar Diggs is the great and powerful wizard they've been waiting for to bring them peace and has positioned herself as an outcast to the Emerald City.
Toad Liu Hai is an ancient spirit of chance and fortune who appears in the DuckTales reboot.

Typhon, also known as the Father of All Monsters, is a major antagonist from Hercules: The Animated Series. He was the most powerful of all the Titans. He was challenged by Zeus and beaten by Hera when she hurled a Thunderbolt at one of Typhon's nostrils. He was imprisoned under Mount Etna, resulting in him gaining a massive headache lasting centuries, during which he sought revenge on Zeus.

Venom, also called the Venom Symbiote, is a character from Marvel Comics. It is a Symbiote, an alien lifeform capable of infusing itself with its host body. When the symbiote bonds with a human, that new dual lifeform refers to itself as Venom. Venom was created by Todd McFarlane and David Michelinie.

Victor Krane is the main antagonist of Disney XD's Lab Rats. He is the mysterious masked man who worked for Douglas Davenport until Krane went behind his back and genetically engineered children with bionic abilities. He was the main antagonist of Season 3, and he still casts his influence/legacy in Season 4. He also started the Bionic War in the episode Rise of the Secret Soldiers. He makes a return in Space Colony, trying to inject liquid bionics into the colonists, and after a while, he is killed by Adam, Bree, and Chase, ending his legacy.

Ventus, or Ven for short, is one of the protagonists of the Kingdom Hearts series who made his debut in Kingdom Hearts: Birth by Sleep. He was a Keyblade wielder who studied with Aqua and Terra long before Sora. Although cheerful and bright, Ventus holds a mysterious past he seeks to recover on his quest to become a Keyblade Master. What he finds is his dark connection with Vanitas, and a more vital one he once made with Sora. Ventus' heart lied within Sora until it rejoined with his proper body once more.

Winifred "Winnie" Sanderson is the main antagonist of Disney's 1993 film Hocus Pocus and its 2022 sequel. She is the eldest and most intelligent witch who lived during the time of , along with her two sisters: Mary and Sarah. For her witchcraft, she was sentenced to death by the Salem townsfolk in 1693 but later brought back from the dead by Max Dennison after three hundred years. Upon her return, Winifred began to terrorize the town in hopes of kidnapping children and stealing their souls to keep herself from dying and aging once more.

Wilkins is a character from the 2016 Disney live-action film Alice Through the Looking Glass. He is a diminutive, metal-mustached Second who works at Time's Castle, trying to keep the universe in balance by checking on the Grand Clock of All Time, especially whenever time starts acting strangely as well as leading an army of clocklike robots known as "Seconds".

Woody, also known as Experiment 507, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to eat wood at a rapid pace. His one true place is with Mrs. Hasagawa as one of her "cats".
Zelda is a character who appears in Spooky Buddies. She is a sorceress and fortune teller. She assists the Buddies when they talk to her about a "ghost" problem.

Zhan Tiri is the main antagonist of Tangled: The Series. She is a power-hungry shapeshifting sorceress, who dreams to gain the full control over the Sundrop and Moonstone. Once a trusted ally of engineer Lord Demanitus, Zhan Tiri engaged in war with him, until the inventor was able to imprison her within an alternate dimension to prevent her from gaining the power of the two elements. As the centuries passed, everyone came to believe that Zhan Tiri was a demonic and unstoppable warlock, while she herself patiently waited for any opportunity to break out from her prison and claim the powers of the Sundrop and Moonstone.

The Bowcien is a character from Mario Tennis Aces. It is the game's final boss. The monster was created when King Bowser grabbed the Lucien. He fused his power with the malefic racket, becoming grey and metallic in the process. ja:エスタークッパ

Fake Yoshis (also called Copycat Yoshis or Phony Yoshis) are a type of Shy Guy that possesses the ability to transform into a Yoshi complete with a fake Baby Mario on his back first appearing in Yoshi's New Island. In their true form, they are Shy Guys wearing green and white robes (in the same color of a Yoshi Egg) but then quickly transform into a duplicate of Yoshi and Baby Mario mimicking all his movements in the same way he moves (although the Fake Yoshis are unable to Flutter Jump and will descend in a failed attempt to do so). As Fake Yoshis are typically closed off, they’re usually harmless.

Li'l Brrs, (also called Brr Bits), are ice enemies that primarily appear in Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2. They are icy crystal-like creatures that vent out clouds of ice from their heads. Li'l Brrs are often seen lingering around however if Mario/Luigi approaches them, they ignite their icy cloud from their head and start chasing the plumbers. To defeat one, Mario/Luigi will need to use a Star Spin to put out the icy cloud surrounding it, from there, it will fall to the ground stunned. If the plumbers are not quick to hit the Brrr Bit while it is vulnerable, it will start to hop around, attempting to jump into Icy Water and regenerate its ice cloud. Li'l Cinders are the fiery

Mad Goombas are a variant of Goomba in Super Princess Peach. They are a type Goombas that is native to Vibe Island and due to its magic, are permanently angry. Their outside appearance is the same as a normal Goomba, but they are reddish with an angry expression. When they stomp their feet, an earthquake follows, stunning Peach temporarily if she is nearby. Mad Goombas aren’t very strong enemies however and virtually any attack can destroy them. The blue Sad Goombas are the opposite of the Mad Goombas.
A White Magikoopa is a white-robed Magikoopa that primarily appear in the Mario role-playing games. They first appear in Paper Mario.
Z-Yuxes are enemies which appear in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. They can summon Mini-Z-Yuxes to guard them.

Cybele the Sorceress is a character in Mario and the Incredible Rescue. She is an old woman with glittering green eyes, living in a cottage in a forest she appears to own. She owned The Book of Spells, which Bowser stole during the events of the book. When she first meets Mario and Luigi, she tells the brothers that they have to give her something so that she may help them. Luigi hands her a coin that he found in the Kero Sewers. Then, she helps Mario and him in saving the Mushroom Kingdom and Princess Peach from Bowser by telling the brothers how to stop Bowser and his spells: The brothers must gather six mushrooms scattered around the Mushroom Kingdom. Cybele gives Mario a blue pouch to ca

Monty Mole Swoopers are Monty Moles fused with Swoopers that appear in volume 5 of Super Mario-kun. They mostly look like Monty Moles, but their arms are replaced with the wings of the Swoopers. Their design when eating the mushroom gives them a mushroom on their head, but their belly pattern and the claws on their feet are removed. After Luigi knocks Mario into the Monty Moles, the Monty Moles call in a group of Swoopers to fuse with them. They quickly eat Mario (who was a mushroom for the majority of the volume), turning him back to normal but giving them the powers of the mushroom instead. They then call in the cow and pig to ram into Mario, Luigi and Yoshi. Mario then sees a Rotating Blo

Mr. Pipe is a Warp Pipe character that appears in Yoshi's New Island, usually as a small Warp Pipe near the beginning of a level or a Checkpoint Ring. He aids a Yoshi and Baby Mario by giving them Flutter Wings, Golden Flutter Wings, and eggs if they lose a specific level. During boss fights, he assists them by throwing eggs or coins if a Yoshi has the maximum number of eggs, and he jumps away. At the end of the game, he is revealed to be adult Mario disguised as a Warp Pipe.

Mr. Anderson is a character and remote helper of Santa Claus appearing in the Saturday Supercade episode "A Christmas Story." He is the owner of Mr. Anderson's Toy Shop. He first appears when Donkey Kong Jr. and Bones Bailey stop by his house to fix their broken motorcycle. When the former asks how he makes many of his toys, he shows them his toy-making machine and demonstrates it by having it print a working set of windup toy soldiers, impressing the Hobo brothers looking through a window. When the onlookers steal the machine, Mr. Anderson asks for them to bring it back. Mr. Anderson reappears near the end of the episode, where he, Jr., Bones, and the redeemed Hobo brothers pile up their wr

Pakkun Mogura is a fusion of a Venus Fire Trap, Muncher, Nipper Plant, and Monty Mole that appears in volume 9 of Super Mario-kun. Its design resembles the average Mega Mole design seen in Super Mario-kun. However, it has a Piranhacus Giganticus on its head as well as two Venus Fire Traps for hands. After Fire Mario defeats a Piranha Plant family, he uproots the Venus Fire Trap, revealing a bunch of Monty Moles attached to the stem that Yoshi proceeds to eat. The bodies of the Venus Fire Trap and a Monty Mole, Muncher and Nipper Plant are suddenly struck by lightning, fusing them together into the Pakkun Mogura. Mario tries throwing Yoshi at it, but the Pakkun Mogura uses the Piranhacus Giga

Poseidon Koopa is Bowser's alter-ego in the second story arc of Super Mario Kart 2 of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. Like his , he is considered the feared god of the sea, ruler of the Gilgamesh Shotō, but his costume and weapon is instead identical to Yaminorius III, the antagonist of , having a cape adorned with living sea dragon heads, a two-pointed pitchfork that can turn into street signs, and a glass helmet that lets him breathe underwater (while, for Yaminorius, it contained special water to let him live outside the demon world's atmosphere). Ted Bull is a white-suited, cowboy-hatted, and wealthy oil tycoon who owns Bull Oil Company. Claiming he can "smell a gusher a mile away," Ted seems to instinctively know when oil has been struck, or when an oil well runs dry.

Tulio is a plumber appearing in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Zenned Out Mario." During the episode, only his silhouette is seen, leaving his physical appearance mostly a mystery. Prior to events of the episode, Mario had asked his sister out. Angry, Tulio went to find him to pulverize him. Later, Tulio arrives at Mario Brothers Plumbing, where he plans to pulverize him. However, after being ordered by Obi-Wan Cannoli to go home and forget about pulverizing Mario and be lucky that he got rid of his sister, he, sounding hypnotized, calls Mario his friend and leaves. The Senior Engineer is a special Blue Suns mercenary located in the engine room of the MSV Strontium Mule. He is unique in being the only Blue Suns mercenary encountered by Commander Shepard with the ability to use tech attacks. He is killed during a firefight between Shepard and the squad when they reach the engine room of the ship.

The Saboteur is an Outlaw and Roekaar unit. These angara specialize in stripping kinetic barriers to add to their own. Along with other armored mid-tier enemies, Pathfinder Ryder can encounter them in places of medium to heavy resistance or among groups of lesser outlaws while APEX teams can face them on Firebases after defeating previous waves of enemies. Saboteurs can be from either gender.
Asimov-kun (real name Akio Aisaki) is a child prodigy who created Boss Borot and several other robots based off of him.

Garadoublas was a mechanical god of the Mycenae Empire. It was regarded as a "Hero" in its time, much like Mazinger Z is to the modern day Japanese population. Its body was eventually recovered by Dr. Hell, and became the basis of Garada K7 and Doublas M2.
Harkenschmitt X9 is a Mechanical Beast used by Count Brocken in his final attempt at revenge against the Mazinger Angels.
Raigon was a large termite-like insect type Warrior Beast. It was a combination of a brother and sister with their true faces located on its antenna.
Abraham was a cyborg commander of Desperado Enforcement LLC. His cyborg serial number was 573 52203 2617.
John was a cyborg commander of World Marshal Inc. His cyborg serial code was 573 52229 2617.
Richard was a high-ranking peace officer within the Denver Police Department, as well as a cyborg commander of World Marshal Inc. His cyborg serial code was 573 52212 2617.
The Evoker King was an advanced artificial intelligence, and the main antagonist of the Minecraft: Woodsword Chronicles series of chapter books.
Kimimaro rushes at his opponent, and using them as support, jumps over them, and grows bone spikes from his back, hitting them at once. pt-br:Amieiro
Pain runs to an opponent and stabs them with his black receiver, messing with their actions.
In their transformed state, a Tenrō clan shinobi can shoot their hair like needles in all directions.

This is a murder-suicide technique. The user creates threads of chakra that are used to connect the user's heart to another person's. As long as the two are connected, any internal damage done to one will also be done to the other. This ultimately means that, if one person dies, so will the other. Only a kunai wrapped in a special Fūma clan tag can safely cut the threads and separate the two.

The ninneko creates a decoy of itself made out of cat food, which dissolves when struck. It apparently must be built beforehand, which the user switches places with when they wish to use it. pt-br:Clone de Ração de Gato

This technique allows the user to temporarily enhance the normal growth of the nails on both their hands and feet, causing them to grow considerably longer in a short space of time as a result. It also seemingly enhances the durability of the nails, allowing them to even clash against swords without breaking.
Haku creates a single ice wall that he can use to push back his opponent or defend against attacks for a short time.

This technique lets the user condense mud or stone from the ground and shape it into spikes that protrude from the ground in order to skewer the target. The spikes cannot penetrate targets of greater density. In the anime, this technique can also produce a single spike, allowing it to be used as a makeshift knife.
Gaara manipulates his sand to create a small body of sand in mid air and cause it to come crashing down into the opponent.

Kabuto slashes his opponent with a chakra scalpel, and with three strikes from his navel snake. Three giant white snakes emerge from the ground in sequence, each biting his opponent, and in the end, four of those emerge behind Kabuto, raise themselves high, and lunge at his opponent.
Hanzō summons Ibuse from the ground, who launches a poison cloud, which travels in a straight line and poisons his opponent by enveloping them. pl:Ibuse no Dokugiri
The user is able to create excrete webbing from the palms of their hands, extending their reach mainly for restraining and trapping their target.

This technique uses the entire body as a spring, by amassing power through taking a posture where the back of the body falls down. With this powerful taijutsu, the user kicks just above the head. Because the power of the kick from the ground is instantly converted into a blow, the enemy hit with this attack will be launched high into the sky. This technique can also be initiated while mid-air.

Karin uses her Mind's Eye of the Kagura to sense her opponent at a long range, alerting her whenever her opponent uses projectile attacks. This prevents her from being hit by their projectile attacks.
With the flick of their wrist the user is capable of firing countless small sparks of lightning towards a target.
An illusion that relies on the sound of the flute. After the user plays a melody though the flute, whoever hears it will become paralysed as if their bodies became heavier.
Using his signature genjutsu, Gengo suppresses the will of his followers and forces them to attack his opponent with taijutsu.

Tsunade enters Sannin Mode and punches her enemy's abdomen (warning them to brace themselves) with such might that in slow motion it appears as though he or she will be snapped in two. They're pushed backwards at tremendous speed, however, razing through a field of trees until they're finally stopped by a large boulder, which causes Tsunade's opponent to take even more damage. Shortly afterwards, a volcano erupts in the background as a result of the punch's power, dyeing the battlefield crimson. Tsunade, straightening herself up, is left wondering whether she perhaps went too far. es:Poder de la Hokage pl:Hokage no Chikara

A tenet of shinobi is that they must escape any situation, no matter how difficult things may seem. Accordingly, this is the first jutsu taught in Konohagakure's Ninja Academy. When the user is bound, they do what they can to escape, such as by finding a way to untie the knot or dislocating their joints in order to get free of the bindings. Although this is the most basic of the escape-based jutsu, it is still fairly complicated to perform. At first, Naruto appeared not to know how to use the technique.

Gaara sends two streams of sand towards the opponent, one stream rises into the sky while the other slides through the ground. The sand stream on the ground hits the opponent and carries him up into the air. Once in midair both streams collide with each other, making the opponent the epicentre of the collision.
Gaara manipulates his sand to create multiple arms of Shukaku rise from the ground and converge on the opponent crushing them into the ground.

After throwing prayer beads on the sealed victim, Chūkaku begins to mumble words while performing ritual hand movements, leading the seal formula to slowly disappear.
